name: Dana Yilmaz

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What is an ordinary shift like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and lead a powder-coating line for bicycle frames. My two-year technical diploma covered oven settings and coating thickness, and the younger operators bring me frames with hard-to-find thin patches. I like a smooth finish; scraping baked powder from a jammed hanger is the part that wears me out.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How are things at home, and do you use AI?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner repairs musical instruments. We have two school-age children, a mortgage and about ten months of expenses saved. My operator rate is high for this job and there are plenty of similar coating shops nearby. I use AI now and then to summarise faults after the fitter checks the note.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the coating crew a neat AI order sheet is welcome, but bicycle frames still need an even finish. The first frame after a powder change gets a real thickness check. I would say that at our union meeting as well.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I lead the powder-coating line and earn more than the usual operator rate. My partner repairs musical instruments, and we have two children in school and a mortgage. We have about ten months of expenses saved and plenty of similar shops nearby. Present income feels sound.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep setting the coating oven and measuring the first frame with a thickness gauge. I use AI now and then to summarise fault notes after the maintenance fitter verifies them. At the next union meeting I'll bring the overspray figures and ask that paid first-frame checking time stays on the shift sheet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. The mortgage is covered and the work still needs a careful eye. A useful note is not worth a spoiled frame.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which coating fault did you catch?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A new blue powder looked even until a frame came out with a thin patch behind the seat tube. We held the batch and reset the spray nozzle. A bicycle frame with a thin coating starts rusting where nobody looks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How do the two wages support home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My factory pay covers most of our household bills; the instrument repairs add a steadier second stream in busy months. We saved the ten-month cushion over several years. The children still need school clothes, so I check the bills before spending on a new oven at home.

say: An **AI order sheet** cannot guarantee even bicycle-frame coating.
Paid **first-frame checks** should stay on the shift sheet.
think: My **higher operator wage** and ten-month reserve cover bills.
The **instrument repairs** and plentiful nearby shops add options.
do: **Keep** gauging the first coated bicycle frame each changeover.
**Bring** overspray figures to the union meeting for paid inspection time.
feel: **Calm** about current household money and work.
S0.quote: A bicycle frame with a thin coating starts rusting where nobody looks.
fieldNote: Dana uses AI **occasionally** for fitter-verified notes, with a physical thickness gauge deciding quality.
Her **union request** concerns actual paid checking time; high pay and a long reserve support calm.

steps.text: Keep gauging first coated bicycle frames after powder changes
Bring overspray figures to union meeting on paid frame checks

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AI may plan powder orders and inspection notes before robots handle hanging frames. The plant should test any camera with known bad coatings on paid time. Our union should see the crew roster before a production target changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would accept a camera that catches real thin spots, but management might use faster inspection to merge two paid lines. Ten months saved gives us room, and many coaters are nearby, but I would not assume another plant matches my higher rate. A real roster cut would affect the mortgage plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll bring the proposed paid roster to the union committee and compare it with three wage slips. If the plant offers a paid guarded trial with a trainer, I'll practise the camera reject on a faulty frame. If my base shifts are actually cut, I'll check posted local coating jobs and apply only where regular pay and school pickup fit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the possible loss of the higher shift rate, though I can inspect the evidence. We can pay bills while I compare options.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you prove the camera works?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd prepare one frame with a deliberately thin patch and one with too much powder at a joint. A trainer should show the safe conveyor stop before I adjust a reject setting. I would not test a live customer's frame first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask at the committee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The union committee should ask how many paid operators remain and who checks frames after the camera rejects one. I would compare base hours, not a good month of overtime. A faster line is not a raise if it removes a paid shift.

say: **AI planning** may reach orders before robots hang frames.
A **camera trial** needs known bad coatings and paid safety time.
think: A merged **coating roster** might cut my higher-rate hours.
Ten months saved and **many shops** give search time, not equal pay.
do: **Bring** paid roster evidence to the union committee.
**Practise** camera rejects if a paid guarded trainer trial is offered.
**Apply** to posted safe local coating if base hours fall and pay and pickup fit.
feel: **Anxious** about realistic high-rate hour loss with a financial buffer.
S1.quote: A faster line is not a raise if it removes a paid shift.
fieldNote: Her **steady adaptation** waits for a known-defect test and offered paid guarded camera practice.
The **union committee** compares actual paid posts, while any local job application requires an hour cut and suitable base pay.

steps.text: Bring written paid roster and wage slips to union committee
Practise camera rejects if paid guarded trainer-led trial offered
Apply for posted safe local coating if base hours cut, pay and pickup fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the coating crew thinking AI could plan frame orders by 2028, then capable robots around 2031 could hang, spray and check the frames. I would ask the union for a written staffing and pay agreement. People need a date, not just a robot brochure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 48 when robots can do the physical coating. My higher-paid shift could go if the plant merges lines, and the instrument shop alone would not carry the mortgage. Ten months saved and plenty of local coaters give a search window; I do not know whether any offer would match my rate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll ask the union committee this month to bargain for notice and offered paid training. If the plant offers a funded paid-time qualification in coating inspection with a guarded trainer place, I'll enrol. If my hours fall, I'll apply to posted safe local coating jobs only if base pay and school hours fit; after qualifying, I'll also apply to posted local inspection roles under the same terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the high wage, but able to compare real offers without missing next month's mortgage payment. Ten months of savings buys time to compare coating jobs, not a promise of equal pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should coating-inspection training include?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The practical exam should include measuring a thin patch behind a frame tube and stopping the conveyor before touching a spray nozzle. A trainer must watch the safety stop. I would not take an inspection certificate based only on slides.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes another shop worth applying to?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would check the posted base rate and shift start, plus travel costs. A shop can pay more per hour and still leave less after fuel and school care. I would apply only when the numbers work for us.

say: **2028 thinking AI** changes orders before robots coat frames around 2031.
The **union agreement** needs written notice and paid training.
think: At **48**, my higher-paid coating shift could disappear.
Ten months saved and **many local coaters** permit search without equal-pay guarantees.
do: **Ask** union committee for written notice and paid training.
**Enrol** in funded paid guarded inspection if offered.
**Apply** to posted safe local coating or qualified inspection if cut, net pay and school fit.
feel: **Anxious** about possible high-wage loss with real options.
S2.quote: Ten months of savings buys time to compare coating jobs, not a promise of equal pay.
fieldNote: She sees **high-rate job risk** without assuming certain loss; a ten-month buffer and numerous shops keep control plausible.
The **coating fallback** and qualified inspection application require real safe local postings, net pay after travel and school-compatible shifts.

steps.text: Ask union committee for written robot notice and funded training
Enrol in coating inspection if funded paid guarded trainer place offered
Apply for posted safe local coating if hours cut, net pay and school hours fit
Apply for posted safe local inspection if qualified, hours cut, net pay and school hours fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI could handle frame orders in 2031, and capable robots could coat them around 2034. Five years lets us teach inspection on a real conveyor. I want a funded place and a posted job, separately.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 51 when physical robots arrive. The children will be older, but the mortgage may remain. A paid inspection certificate could help, yet other plants may use robots too. We can save from higher wages while shifts last.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll add new money from each full higher-rate payday to our reserve after bills. I'll ask the plant for a recognized coating-test certificate with covered fees, paid release and supervised guarded practice. If an actual seat is offered, I'll enrol; once qualified, if coating hours shrink, I'll apply for posted safe local quality work only if net regular pay and school travel fit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the later crew change, with time to check pay and training. I can stay on this line while I look.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the coating-test exam require?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The test should make me use a thickness gauge, reject a corrodible corner and isolate the conveyor. The trainer needs to sign the practice on the machine. I would not learn from an unpaid video at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you compare quality postings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The posting should state regular pay, paid travel and actual shift times. If a farther shop takes away too much time or fuel, I would stay put. A mortgage deserves a posted coating-quality wage, not a hopeful job title.

say: **2031 thinking AI** changes orders before robots coat frames around 2034.
A **funded practical seat** is separate from a posted job.
think: At **51**, I may still need a mortgage wage.
Full higher-rate shifts could grow **new savings** before robot changes.
do: **Save** new money from full higher-rate pay after bills.
**Enrol** in coating inspection if funded paid guarded practice offered.
**Apply** for posted safe local quality if qualified, hours shrink, net pay and school travel fit.
feel: **Anxious** about future wage risk with time to verify terms.
S3.quote: A mortgage deserves a posted coating-quality wage, not a hopeful job title.
fieldNote: Her **new deposits** come from future full higher-rate pay, while the course requires funded fees and paid guarded practice.
The **quality application** follows qualification and reduced hours, with a posted safe local role at adequate net pay and family travel.

steps.text: Save new money from full higher-rate coating wages after bills
Enrol in coating test if funded paid guarded practical place offered
Apply for posted safe local quality if qualified, hours shrink, net pay and school travel fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI could plan frame orders by 2036, with capable robots coating around 2039. A decade gives the union time to bargain for real technical jobs and paid apprenticeships. The young crew should know what a posted role pays.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 56 when robots do the physical work. The children may be grown, but I will not assume the mortgage is paid. Ten months saved now and plenty of local coaters give room to choose if wages and safe jobs remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep the coating line and pay extra mortgage principal from newly earned full-wage months after bills. I'll attend the union committee each quarter to ask for offered paid maintenance seats and actual postings. If a funded paid guarded place with a trainer is offered, I'll take it; after qualifying, if coating hours fall, I'll apply for posted safe local maintenance only when net base pay and travel work at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the far-off line change, while current higher wages remain. I can prepare without spending a sound wage on a course brochure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the union agreement need to say?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The agreement should say how many paid technical posts remain, who pays during supervised practice and what the safety test covers. I would ask for the figures before a vote. A training promise with no paid seat leaves an operator on the same old line.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make a maintenance offer viable?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare the maintenance posting's base rate after fuel with our mortgage and school routine. A maintenance title with too many unpaid travel hours could pay less than my coating shift. I would keep the coating shift until a signed offer made sense.

say: **2036 thinking AI** changes orders before robots coat frames around 2039.
The union should bargain for **real technical posts** and paid seats.
think: At **56**, I might still need a mortgage wage.
Ten months saved and **many coaters** help if job pay holds.
do: **Pay** extra mortgage principal from newly earned wages after bills.

feel: **Uneasy** about distant robots with current wages secure.
S4.quote: A maintenance title with too many unpaid travel hours could pay less than my coating shift.
fieldNote: She uses **quarterly union talks** to connect actual paid training places with posted technical roles.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which worries you most, and what would help?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The fast 2028 case worries me most because capable robots around 2031 could cut our higher-paid coating shift before another rate is clear. Written notice, an offered funded paid practical seat and a posted safe local job at enough net base pay would help. I'd bring the terms to the union.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who measures the first frame after a robot changes the powder. A rusty bicycle frame is a defect that can wait months to show itself.

headlineQuote: A rusty bicycle frame is a defect that can wait months to show itself.
portrait: **Dana**, 43, is a skilled senior bicycle-frame coating lead with a two-year technical diploma and higher pay.
She and her instrument-repair partner support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage, with ten months saved and many nearby shops.
Her **progressive outlook** leads to union committee work, while she tests proven tools and uses AI only occasionally.
Fast robots make her **anxious** about losing the higher rate; paid training and net local pay shape her choices.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could bring capable coating robots around 2031 and put her higher-paid shift at risk.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, funded paid practical training and posted safe local work with enough net base pay would help.
